title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

reports.title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

summary:
Matthew and Leah Spurlock were pulled over in Colwich, Kansas, after a Flock camera flagged their minivan as possibly stolen. Their KU Alumni plate had the number 7007, and a stolen GMC pickup had a temporary Kansas tag with the same number but a different background. Police learned the wrong plate type had been entered into the system. About a month later, in Catoosa, Oklahoma, another Flock camera led police to stop them at gunpoint and handcuff Matthew before the mistake was sorted out.

Kansas duplicates plate numbers across more than 100 designs, about half of them specialty plates, and Flock cameras read only letters and numbers, not plate backgrounds. Wichita police Capt. Casey Slaughter said such alerts are not enough alone to stop a car, but a confirmed stolen tag leaves little recourse. Kansas is moving from six digit to seven digit non duplicated plate numbers, and Wichita police have discussed training Flock to recognize plate backgrounds. The Spurlocks' stolen vehicle entry has expired, so they no longer expect stops.
